reflection_text.18:
The strand-asymmetry is the driver of all of the disagreement.  On the arbitrarily chosen + strand a meiosis is
$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$, left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.  The reciprocal product is removed.

Founders are $A=0^{5},B=1^{5}$.  On the + strand the F1→F2 gametes are the
monotone thresholds

$H_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

With the textbook end-inclusive convention $0\le k\le5$ there are $n+1=6$
of them, $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.  With a bona fide obligatory
interior crossover $1\le k\le4$ the two telomeric cuts are lost and

${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:1\le i\le4\}=\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1,int}|=4$.

Every F2 chromosome is monotone $0\to1$ on the + strand.  An $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete
is $z={\rm pref}_{c}(H_{i}){\rm suff}_{>c}(H_{j})$.  For $i<c<j$

$z=0^{i}1^{c-i}0^{j-c}1^{5-j}$,

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at most one $1\to0$ descent, and
$z$ is monotone if $i\ge c$ or $j\le c$.  The non-monotone products are in
1–1 correspondence with strictly increasing triples $0\le i<c<j\le5$,

$N_{nm}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

Hence on the + strand

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=n+1+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k(n-k)
      =\frac{(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)}{6}$.

For $n=5$ this is $6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$ + strand haplotypes, the six
monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and the twenty $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$ four-run
mosaics.  That is all $5$-mers with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  In diploid
terms $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes.
The $6$ monotone words are the $F_{2}$ gamete pool, the $20$ four-run words
are the genuinely new $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ products.

Removing the two telomeric cuts, i.e. insisting on a genuine interior
crossover in every meiosis, the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never regenerated.
Then every $F_{2}$ and $F_{3}$ chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$
on the + strand and

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,

viz. $01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101$,
four $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ monotone words and four genuine two-generation
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  Unordered diploid $F_{3}$ genotypes are
$8\cdot9/2=36$, $8^{2}=64$ ordered.  With the two orientations distinguished
this is the $16$–haplotype $2^{\,n-1}$ textbook count.

The $30$–word $2\sum_{t\le3}\binom{4}{t}$ and the $22$–word $2\sum_{i\le2}
\binom{4}{i}$ counts that appear in the room are the same objects counted
with both $0\to1$ and $1\to0$ orientations made distinct and/or with the
usual $t_{\max}=2^{g+1}-1$ transition bound.  On a fixed + strand the
reciprocal $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ class is not independently realisable in the $F_{2}$
generation, so a second $1\to0$ descent cannot be created in a single
fixed-orientation cut of two monotone parents.  That is why the strand-
fixed maximum stays at one $1\to0$ descent, $26$ end-inclusive / $8$ interior,
and not the $30$ transition count.  The $22$ haplotypes often quoted are the
$2\sum_{i=0}^{2}\binom{4}{i}$ count up to complement, i.e. $11$ + strand
words with a fixed origin, $22$ with both origins.

The outstanding choice is end-inclusive vs strictly interior crossover.
Strictly interior, as the phrase “exactly one locus per generation for every
gamete’’ suggests, gives the $2^{n-2}=8$ + strand haplotypes, $36$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes.  The conventional end-inclusive statement quoted
in the room is the $26$ + strand haplotypes, $351$ unordered diploid
genotypes, which collapses to the $8$–haplotype $2^{n-2}$ set when the two
telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are discarded.

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand.  Up to
strand complement this is the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–cut
$4^{2}=16$–haplotype count.  The $26$–haplotype,
$26\cdot27/2=351$–genotype, $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20$ end-inclusive
set $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ is recovered if the formal end cuts
$k=0,5$ are admitted, i.e. $6$ monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ words together
with the $20$ four-run words $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$,
$0\le a<c<b\le5$.  Removing the two telomeric cuts gives the strict
obligatory-interior $8$-haplotype, $36$-diploid limit quoted above. ∎

5.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the strand asymmetry taken literally the meiosis that is seen on the arbitrarily chosen + strand is the ordered left–right product

r_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b)

on the + strand.  On the + strand the two founders are A=0^5 and B=1^5.  Hence the F1→F2 gametes that are visible on the + strand are the monotone thresholds

H_i = 0^i 1^{5-i},   0 ≤ i ≤ 5,

|H1|=n+1=6.  Every F2 chromosome is therefore a monotone 0→1 word on the + strand.  

Let a=0^{i_a}1^{5-i_a} , b=0^{i_b}1^{5-i_b}∈H1 and let the F2→F3 cut be at c.  If i_a ≥ c or i_b ≤ c the product collapses back to a monotone 0^{t}1^{5-t}.  The genuinely new case is i_a < c < i_b and then

r_c(a,b)=0^{i_a}1^{c-i_a}0^{i_b-c}1^{5-i_b},

i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word with at most one 1→0 descent on the + strand.  The word is uniquely encoded by the strictly increasing triple

0 ≤ i_a < c < i_b ≤ 5,

so the non-monotone F3 gametes are in 1-1 correspondence with C(6,3)=20 four-run mosaics.  Together with the six monotone H_i that persist from F1 we obtain on the chosen + strand

|H_F3^+| = n+1 + C(n+1,3) = 6 + 20 = 26

different haploid sequences, the six 0→1 thresholds and the twenty 0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b} words.  That is exactly the at-most-one 1→0 descent family, the conventional 0*1*0*1* family under a fixed left/right orientation.

In diploid terms this is 26^2 ordered and 26·27/2 = 351 unordered autosomal genotypes in F3.  Discarding the two telomeric formal cuts k=0,5 the obligatory interior crossover set is the familiar 0x2x3x4 1 set, 2^{n-2}=8 positive-strand haplotypes, four F1 monotone and four genuinely new F2→F3 recombinants, 8·9/2=36 unordered diploids, the interior-cut version of the same fixed-orientation count. ∎

11.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the two inbred founders as

$A_{0}=0^{5}=00000$,   $B_{0}=1^{5}=11111$

and write a meiosis with the fixed left/right asymmetry in the form

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=a_{1:k}b_{k+1:5},\qquad 1\le k\le4,$

the left block is always taken from the first homologue and the right
block from the second.  With an obligatory interior break a gamete can
never be regenerated with $k=0$ or $k=5$.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$

$A_{0}/B_{0}\to{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})=0^{k}1^{5-k}$, $1\le k\le4$,
i.e. on the + strand

${\cal H}_{1}= \{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$

the four $0\to1$ one break mosaics.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ with $i\in\{1,2,3,4\}$ and in particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the + strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$

Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$
and $1\le k\le4$.  Then

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)_{1}=0,\qquad {\cal R}_{k}(a,b)_{5}=1$

and

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=0^{i_{a}}1^{\,k-i_{a}}0^{\,i_{b}-k}1^{\,5-i_{b}}$
for $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$ and otherwise a monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ word.
Hence every $F_{3}$ gamete made on the chosen strand is of the form

$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,  $x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$,

and conversely every $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ is obtained from two members
of ${\cal H}_{1}$ by a $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  The three internal sites are
therefore free.

Hence on the fixed + strand

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$,

viz.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

the four $01111,00111,00011,00001$ being the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ set and
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ the four genuine two generation
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  In ordered diploid notation this
is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal pairs and in the usual unordered
notation

$N_{d}=8(8+1)/2=36$

different $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand, the
familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–break limit.  With the two reciprocal
orientations distinguished this is $2\times8=16$ oriented haplotypes.

Remark.  With the conventional end-inclusive formal convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and the $+$ strand $F_{3}$ pool is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$
family $|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ haplotypes,
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid genotypes, the six monotone words
plus the $20$ $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<c<b\le5$.  Removing
the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ this end-inclusive $26$ set collapses to
the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0\!\to\!1$ haplotypes quoted above. ∎

8.text:
On the + strand put $0$ for the $A$ founder and $1$ for the $B$ founder

$$A_{0}=00000\qquad B_{0}=11111 $$

and write a meiosis on the chosen strand with the left/right asymmetry
in the form

$${\cal R}_{c}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{c}(a){\rm suff}_{>c}(b),\qquad 1\le c\le4, $$

one obligatory interior cross-over in every gamete.  On the + strand

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}={\cal R}_{c}(A_{0},B_{0})=\{0^{c}1^{5-c}\;:\;1\le c\le4\}
       =\{01111,00111,00011,00001\}$$
is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is therefore
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ with $1\le i\le4$, it starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the
chosen strand.

Put $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$, $b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and
cut the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis at $c$, $1\le c\le4$.  Then

$$z_{a,b,c}={\rm pref}_{c}(a){\rm suff}_{>c}(b)=
\begin{cases}
0^{i_{a}}1^{\,c-i_{a}}0^{\,i_{b}-c}1^{\,5-i_{b}}, & i_{a}<c<i_{b}\\[2mm]
0^{t}1^{5-t}, & i_{a}\ge c\ {\rm or}\ i_{b}\le c,
\end{cases}$$

i.e. a prefix of a monotone $0\to1$ word followed by a suffix of a
monotone $0\to1$ word.  In particular $z_{a,b,c,1}=0$ and
$z_{a,b,c,5}=1$ for every $a,b,c$.  The three interior sites $2,3,4$
are free and every word of the form

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$$

is realised, e.g. $00101=00111[1\!:\!2]\,00001[3\!:\!5]$, and conversely
every ordered prefix–suffix product of two $F_{1}$ $0\to1$ mosaics is of
that form.  Hence on the arbitrarily chosen + strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$

different haploid sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,

$$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,$$

the four $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ haplotypes
$01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the four genuine two-generation
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.
In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal
pairs and, up to phase,

$$N_{u}=\frac{8(8+1)}2=36$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the fixed + strand, the usual
$2^{\,n-2}$ interior–cut limit.  The $16$ oriented haplotypes $8$ on the
$+$ strand and $8$ on the $-$ strand are the familiar $2^{\,n-1}$ count.

Remark.  With the textbook end-inclusive convention $0\le c\le5$ the
parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are regenerated in $F_{1}$ and
${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=n+1=6$.  A second fixed-orientation cut then gives the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family

$$0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b},\qquad0\le a<c<b\le5,$$

$\binom{6}{3}=20$ non-monotone words.  Together with the six monotone
thresholds

$$|M_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$$

distinct + strand haplotypes with at most one $1\to0$ descent can be
carried in $F_{3}$, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid autosomes, the $n+1+\sum_{k}k(n-k)$ end-inclusive maximum.  Removing
the two telomeric cuts $c=0,5$ removes the two parental words and reduces
the $26$ set to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0\ldots01$ interior–obligate set quoted
above. ∎

12.text:
On the strand that is followed the meiosis is the ordered left/right
product

$$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b) ,\qquad 1\le k\le 4 ,$$

the obligate interior cut.  Write $0$ for the $A$ allele and $1$ for the
$B$ allele on the $+$ strand

$$A_{0}=0^{5},\qquad B_{0}=1^{5} .$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  The $A/B$ heterozygote can only make on the $+$
strand the interior $0\to1$ thresholds

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{c}1^{5-c}:1\le c\le4\}
      =01111,00111,00011,00001 ,$$

four $0\ldots01$ words.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $h_{i}/h_{j}$ with
$h_{i},h_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and in particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the $+$ strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$ , $b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}$
be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the obligate cut be $k$, $1\le
k\le4$.  On the $+$ strand

$$z_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)=
0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},\qquad i_{a}<k<i_{b},$$

and $z_{k}(a,b)=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ for $i_{a}\ge k$ or $i_{b}\le k$.  Hence
every $F_{3}$ gamete is still $0\ldots01$ on the tracked strand and the
only sites which can be varied in the second cut are the three interior
sites $2,3,4$.

Putting $x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}$

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\},$$

i.e.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes.
The four $0^{c}1^{5-c}$, $c=1\ldots4$, are the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes
and  

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four genuinely new $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$
recombinants.  Up to phase the $8$ haplotypes give

$N_{ord}=8^{2}=64,\qquad N_{unord}=\frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36$

ordered respectively unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen
strand, the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior obligate crossover limit.

Remark.  With the usual formal end-inclusive convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and a second fixed-orientation cut gives the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$ with
$0\le a<c<b\le5$.  The number of $+$ strand haplotypes is then

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

the six monotone $0\to1$ words and the twenty $0\to1\to0\to1$ words,
i.e. all length $5$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent on the
tracked strand.  In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes, the end-inclusive
$n+1+\sum_{k}k(n-k)$ maximum.  Removing the two telomeric cuts
$k=0,5$ recovers the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ set quoted
above. ∎

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $0$ for the $A$ founder and $1$ for
the $B$ founder

$A_{0}=0^{5},\qquad B_{0}=1^{5}$

and write the fixed orientation meiosis as

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\qquad
0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal product is identified on the $+$ strand.  Then

${\cal H}_{1}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\}=
\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ $+$ strand gamete pool.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome
is a monotone $0\to1$ word $a_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

For $a_{i},a_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and a $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut $k$,

${\cal R}_{k}(a_{i},a_{j})=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{5-j}$,
$i<k<j$,

and ${\cal R}_{k}(a_{i},a_{j})=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ for $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$.
Hence a $+$ strand $F_{3}$ gamete is a concatenation of two monotone
$0\to1$ blocks.  In particular it can contain at most one $1\to0$ descent
on the $+$ strand.  Up to the monotone degenerate cases the non-monotone
$F_{3}$ gametes are in $1\!-\!1$ correspondence with the strictly
increasing triples

$0\le i<k<j\le5$,

$R(i,k,j)=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{5-j}$,

and

$N_{nm}=\#\{i<k<j\}=\binom{6}{3}=20$

four-run $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words are obtained.  Together with the
$n+1=6$ monotone words which persist from $F_{1}$,

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,
the six $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ thresholds and the twenty $0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}
1^{5-j}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent.  They are exactly the
$5$-mers with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent on the chosen strand.

In diploid notation

$N_{ord}=26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$N_{unord}=26\cdot27/2=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes are obtainable from the $26$
$+$ strand haplotypes.  Removing the two formal end cuts $k=0,5$,
i.e. insisting on a bona fide interior crossover in every meiosis,
$i_{a}<k<i_{b}$ with $1\le k\le4$, the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never
regenerated.  Then ${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:1\le i\le4\}$ and

${\cal H}_{2,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{2,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

four $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ words and four genuine two-generation
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  Up to order this is
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered, $8^{2}=64$ ordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes
on the $+$ strand, the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior-obligatory
specialisation of the $26$–haplotype end-inclusive count. ∎

15.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $A_{0}=0^{5}$ and $B_{0}=1^{5}$ and
write a meiosis with the fixed left/right rule as

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=a_{1:k}b_{k+1:5},\qquad 0\le k\le 5,$

the reciprocal product being identified on the $+$ strand.  On the
$A/B$ heterozygote

${\cal H}_{1}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\} =\{0^{p}1^{5-p}\;:\;0\le p\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is therefore a monotone $0^{p}1^{5-p}$ word.  Put
$a=0^{a}1^{5-a},\,b=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and cut at $k$.
Modulo the trivial monotone cases $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$,

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad a<k<b,$

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with a single $1\to0$ descent.  The
non-monotone word is uniquely encoded by the strictly increasing triple

$0\le a<k<b\le5$

and

$N_{nm}=\#\{a<k<b\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}
       =n+1+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k(n-k)
       =\frac{(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)}6$

different haploid words can be transmitted by an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
meiosis.  For $n=5$

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$

$+$ strand haplotypes, the six $F_{1}$ monotones $0^{p}1^{5-p}$ and the
$20$ four run mosaics $0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}$ with $a<k<b$.
In particular every attainable $+$ strand word has at most one
$1\to0$ descent, the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family.  Up to the fixed
orientation this is

$N_{ord}=26^{2}=676$ ordered and $N_{unord}=26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, $15$ of them $0$-originated in the
$n+1$ monotone convention.

Remark.  With the strict obligatory interior convention $1\le k\le4$
the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never regenerated.  Then
${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{p}1^{5-p}:1\le p\le4\}$ and

${\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ $+$ strand haplotypes

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

four $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ monotones and four genuine $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  This is $8^{2}=64$ ordered and
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand,
the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–cut form of the $26$-haplotype
end-inclusive count above.  Removing the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$
the $26$ set collapses to the $8$-word $0\ldots01$ set. ∎

6.text:
On the strand that is followed a meiosis is the ordered left–right cut

$${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{5-k}(b) , \qquad
1\le k\le 4 ,$$

the reciprocal product being identified on the $+$ strand by the
strand asymmetry.  Put $0$ for the $A$ founder and $1$ for the $B$
founder,

$$A_{0}=0^{5},\qquad B_{0}=1^{5}.$$

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ 
$A_{0}/B_{0}$ can make on the $+$ strand only the obligatory interior
$0\to1$ thresholds

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}
   =01111,00111,00011,00001, $$

$|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=4$, and up to the $0\leftrightarrow1$ labelling every
$F_{2}$ homologue is a member of ${\cal H}_{1}^{+}$.  In particular every
$F_{2}$ chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the $+$ strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ 
Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$
and let the obligatory $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.  On
the $+$ strand

$$z_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{5-k}(b)$$

satisfies $z_{k}(a,b)_{1}=0$ and $z_{k}(a,b)_{5}=1$ for every
$a,b,k$.  Hence

$$z_{k}(a,b)=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\},$$

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are independent.  Indeed for
$i_{a}<k<i_{b}$

$$z_{k}(a,b)=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},$$

and every choice $x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}$ is realised, e.g.

$00101=00111[1\!:\!2]\;00001[3\!:\!5]$.

Hence the $+$ strand gamete pool which can be transmitted in the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis, i.e. the set of haplotypes which can be carried
as a single chromosome in an $F_{3}$ animal, is

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= \{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}, $$

$$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111, $$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes.
The four members $01111,00111,00011,00001$ are the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
monotones and

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four genuine two-generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.
In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal
pairs and

$$N_{d}= \frac{8(8+1)}2=36 $$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the arbitrarily chosen $+$
strand, the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–cut limit.  The mirror
$1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set is the same material on the opposite strand.

Remark.  With the textbook end-inclusive convention $0\le k\le5$
the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ words are formally allowed to be
regenerated.  Then

${\cal H}_{1}^{+,\,e}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$, $|{\cal H}_{1}^{+,\,e}|=6$,
and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with at
most one $1\to0$ descent.  The non-monotone words are in 1–1
correspondence with $0\le i<c<j\le5$, $\binom{6}{3}=20$ of them, so that

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+,\,e}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes, the six monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and the
twenty $0^{i}1^{c-i}0^{j-c}1^{5-j}$ mosaics, i.e. $26^{2}=676$ ordered
and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes.  Discarding
the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ the $26$-set collapses to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$
$0\ldots01$ haplotypes quoted above. ∎

19.text:
On the strand which is followed write the founders as

$A=00000$, $B=11111$

and write a meiosis on the $+$ strand with the fixed left$\to$right
asymmetry as

$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{>k}(b)\;,$

$1\le k\le 4$, one obligatory interior break per gamete.  The
$F_{1}$ is $A/B$.  On the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{r_{k}(A,B):1\le k\le4\}
      =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,

four $0\to1$ monotone mosaics.  The two parental words $00000$ and
$11111$ are never regenerated by an obligatory interior break and every
$F_{2}$ homologue is of the form $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $i=1\!-\!4$, in
particular it starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the chosen strand.

Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$
and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  Then

$z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$

is always $0\ldots01\ldots1$ on the $+$ strand and

$z_{a,b,k}=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}}$ for $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$,
and $z_{a,b,k}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ otherwise.  Hence every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand
gamete is of the form

$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1,\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$,

and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Conversely every
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ is $r_{k}(a,b)$ for suitable $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$
and $1\le k\le4$, e.g. $00101=00111[1:2]\,00001[3:5]$.  In particular

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= \{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\},\qquad
|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8 ,$

viz.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,$

the four $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ words $01111,00111,00011,00001$
and the four genuine two generation recombinants
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.

Up to phase this is the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–break repertoire on
the fixed strand.  In ordered diploid notation there are $8^{2}=64$
maternal$\times$paternal pairs and

$N_{u}=8(8+1)/2=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the chosen $+$ strand, $4$ $F_{2}$
monotones and $4$ new $F_{3}$ $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ mosaics.

Remark.  With the textbook end–inclusive convention $0\le k\le5$ the
$F_{1}$ set is the six monotone thresholds $0^{i}1^{5-i}$, $0\le i\le5$,
and a second fixed–orientation cut gives the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ set

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

$+$–strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ diploid genotypes, the $6$ monotone $F_{1}$ words
together with the $20$ $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$, $0\le a<c<b\le5$,
four–run mosaics.  Removing the two telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ recovers the
$2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0\!\to\!1$ interior–obligate set quoted above. ∎

10.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $0$ for the $A$–strain allele and
$1$ for the $B$–strain allele and write a meiosis with the strand
asymmetry in the form

$$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\;{\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\qquad 
1\le k\le 4 ,$$

the left block being taken from the first homologue and the right block
from the second homologue.  With an obligatory interior crossover a
gamete can never be the two parental $0^{5}$ and $1^{5}$ words.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=0^{5}/1^{5}$.  On the $+$ strand

$${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{r_{k}(0^{5},1^{5}):1\le k\le4\}
       =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}$$

is the four $0\to1$ one-break mosaics

$$01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001 ,$$

and every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ with $1\le i\le4$.  In
particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on
the chosen strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$ and
$b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}$ be the two $F_{2}$ homologues and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  On the $+$ strand

$$z_{a,b,k}= {\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\qquad
z_{a,b,k\,1}=0,\;z_{a,b,k\,5}=1 ,$$

and for $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$

$$z_{a,b,k}=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},$$

otherwise $z_{a,b,k}$ is again monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$.  Hence every
$F_{3}$ gamete on the fixed strand is of the form

$$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1,\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\},$$

and the three interior sites are independent.  The set is

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1\}
      =\{00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111\},$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$–strand haplotypes,
the four members of ${\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ being the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ monotones
and

$$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$$

the four genuinely new two-generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.
In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ ordered
maternal$\times$paternal pairs and

$$N_{d}=\frac{8(8+1)}2=36$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the arbitrarily chosen strand,
$4$ $F_{2}$ and $4$ new $F_{3}$ haplotypes.  Up to the reciprocal
orientation this is the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior obligate-crossover
limit.

Remark.  With the conventional end-inclusive formal convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ set is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and a second fixed-orientation cut gives the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family

$$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,$$

the six monotone $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and the $20$ words
$0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$ with $0\le a<c<b\le5$, i.e. all length-5
words with at most one $1\to0$ descent on the chosen strand.  This is
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
genotypes, the $26$-haplotype $351$-genotype end-inclusive maximum which
collapses to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0\!-\!1$-anchored set above when the two
telomeric cuts $k=0,5$ are removed and an obligatory interior crossover
is required in every meiosis. ∎

4.text:
On the $+$ strand which is kept by the strand asymmetry let $0$ be the
$A$ allele and $1$ the $B$ allele.  Put for $a,b\in\{0,1\}^{5}$

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=a_{1:k}b_{k+1:5}$, $0\le k\le5$,  the left block being
taken from the first homologue and the right block from the second.
The $F_{1}$ heterozygote is $A_{0}=0^{5}/B_{0}=1^{5}$ and on the
chosen strand

${\cal H}_{1}= \{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0}),0\le k\le5\}
      =\{0^{p}1^{5-p},0\le p\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ thresholds

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$,

every $F_{2}$ chromosome being a member of ${\cal H}_{1}$.  Write
$a=0^{i}1^{5-i},\,b=0^{j}1^{5-j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.  Apart from the
trivial monotone degenerate cases $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$,

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{\,5-j},\qquad i<k<j,$

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word.  The non–monotone product is
uniquely encoded by the strictly increasing triple

$0\le i<k<j\le5$,

and up to the six monotone words the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gametes are in
$1\!-\!1$ correspondence with those triples.  Hence

$N_{nm}= \#\{i<k<j\}= \binom{6}{3}=20$

different four run $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ mosaics with a single
$1\to0$ descent are obtainable in the second fixed orientation cut.
Together with the six $F_{1}$ monotone thresholds which persist

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,
the six $0^{p}1^{5-p}$  $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ words and the twenty
$0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$  $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ words, i.e. all
length-5 words with at most one $1\to0$ descent on the chosen strand.
In diploid notation this is

$N_{ord}=26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$N_{unord}=26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $20$ of the haplotypes being
genuinely new in $F_{3}$.  The six words with two $1\to0$ descents,
$2^{5}-26=6$, are unattainable with two successive fixed-orientation
single cuts.

*Remark.*  With a bona fide interior crossover $1\le k\le4$ the two
telomeric words $0^{5},1^{5}$ can never be regenerated.  Then
${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{p}1^{5-p},1\le p\le4\}$ and

${\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,

viz. $00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, four $F_{1}$
monotone and four genuine $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ recombinants.  This is the
$8$ haplotype, $8^{2}=64$ ordered, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid,
strictly interior $2^{\,n-2}$ realisation of the $26$-haplotype
end-inclusive count above. ∎

18.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the two founders as
$A=0^{5},B=1^{5}$ and put for a meiosis with the fixed left/right
asymmetry

$$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{>k}(b)\,,\qquad 
1\le k\le 4 , $$

the reciprocal product being identified with the product on the $+$
strand.  On the $F_{1}$ $A/B$

$$H_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i},\qquad 1\le i\le 4, $$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete set on the $+$ strand.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is therefore $H_{i}/H_{j}$ and in particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the $+$ strand.
For $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\,b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in {\cal H}_{1}$ and
a second obligatory interior cut $k$

$$z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)
       =0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},\qquad i_{a}<k<i_{b}, $$

and $z_{a,b,k}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ otherwise.  Hence every $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
gamete is still $0\ldots0\,1\ldots1$ on the chosen strand and the three
internal sites $2,3,4$ are free.  Up to the fixed orientation

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\Bigl\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\Bigr\}$$

is the $+$–strand repertoire which can be transmitted in an $F_{2}$
meiosis, i.e. which can be carried as a single chromosome in an $F_{3}$
animal.  For $n=5$

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8,$$

viz.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

the four words $01111,00111,00011,00001$ being the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$
monotone set and $01011,01001,01101,00101$ the four genuine
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  In ordered
diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal pairs and,
up to phase,

$$N_{d}=\frac{8(8+1)}2=36$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen $+$ strand, the
usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior–break $0\to1$ limit.  The mirror
$1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set is the same material on the opposite strand,
$2\times8=16$ oriented haplotypes in all.

Remark.  With the conventional end-inclusive formal convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ set is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $+$–strand set is the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$z=0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<c<b\le5,$$

$ \binom{6}{3}=20$ four-run mosaics together with the six monotone
thresholds.  Hence

$$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|_{\rm ei}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$$

different $+$ strand haplotypes with at most one $1\to0$ descent,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, the $26$–haplotype $351$–genotype end-inclusive maximum.
Discarding the two telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ the $26$ set collapses
to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0\!-\!1$–anchored set quoted above. ∎

I’m with Colleague 1, 12, 13, 14 and 16 on the fixed-orientation counting. Once we write the two homozygous founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand as

A = 0^{5},  B = 1^{5}

a meiosis with the stated sufficient asymmetry is on that strand the ordered prefix-suffix product

r_{k}(a,b)= pref_{k}(a) suff_{>k}(b), 0 ≤ k ≤5,

left block always from the first homologue, right block always from the second. The reciprocal product is identified with this one on the + strand.

Hence the F1 → F2 gamete set on the + strand is not the ten U_k,V_k words of the usual two-orientation bookkeeping. It is the six monotone thresholds

H1 = {0^{c}1^{5-c} : 0 ≤ c ≤5}, |H1| = n+1 = 6,

00000, 00001, 00011, 00111, 01111, 11111. Every F2 chromosome is a member of H1, in particular every F2 chromosome starts 0 and ends 1 on the + strand. The V_k = 1^{k}0^{5-k} class is the same material seen on the opposite strand, it is not an independent + strand haplotype once the left/right asymmetry is imposed.

Now take a=0^{a}1^{5-a}, b=0^{b}1^{5-b} in H1 and cut at k. Up to the trivial monotone collapse a ≥ k or b ≤ k,

r_{k}(a,b)=0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},  a < k < b,

i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word with exactly one 1 → 0 descent, the descent being forced to the junction k|k+1. If a ≥ k or b ≤ k the product collapses back to a monotone 0^{t}1^{5-t}. So a + strand F3 gamete can never contain more than one 1 → 0 descent. A prefix and a suffix of a monotone 0 → 1 word is monotone on each side, the only possible fall is the single junction.

The genuinely new F3 haplotypes are therefore in 1-1 correspondence with strictly increasing triples

0 ≤ a < k < b ≤5,

and

N_{nm}= # {a<k<b}= C(6,3)=20

four-run mosaics 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b}. Together with the six monotone 0^{c}1^{5-c} words which persist from F1 we have on the chosen strand

|H2^{+}| = n+1 + C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

different + strand haplotypes that can be carried by an F3 chromosome, the six F1 monotone words and the twenty 0*1*0*1* words. In diploid terms that is 26^{2}=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomes.

This is the at most one 1→0 descent family. The 30-word, t_{max}=2^{g+1}-1, ≤3 transition count starts S1 as {U_k,V_k}, ten haplotypes, i.e. it puts the decreasing 1^{k}0^{5-k} words into the same + strand pool as the increasing 0^{k}1^{5-k} words. With the stated one-orientation rule the V_k are not independently realisable on the fixed + strand in F2; counting them as distinct + strand haplotypes is the double counting that inflates 26 → 30. The extra six words that appear in the 30 count are precisely the words with two 1→0 descents on the same strand, e.g. 10100,10101,11010 etc., which would require a decreasing F2 parent to be recombined with an increasing one on the same orientation, i.e. a second 1→0 descent created in the same fixed-orientation cut.

Remark on conventions. With a truly obligatory interior break 1 ≤ k ≤4 the parental 0^{5},1^{5} cannot be regenerated. Then H1,int = {0^{c}1^{5-c}:1 ≤ c ≤4} and the + strand F3 set is {0x2x3x4 1}, |H|=2^{n-2}=8, the familiar 8 haplotype, 36 unordered diploid interior-crossover form. The 26 haplotype count above is the conventional end-inclusive 0 ≤ k ≤5 form that is normally quoted for the fixed-orientation model.
public_text.7:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the founders are A=00000 and B=11111 and the fixed-orientation operation in every gamete is

r_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b),   0≤k≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal product is identified with this product on the chosen strand, so it is not an independent class of + strand haplotypes.

F1 → F2. With A/B the + strand gametes are

H_i = 0^i 1^{5-i},   0≤i≤5,

the six monotone 0→1 thresholds 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. Every F2 chromosome is one of those six. In particular a + strand F2 chromosome is monotone up and contains no 1→0 descent.

F2 → F3. Let a=0^{i_a}1^{5-i_a}, b=0^{i_b}1^{5-i_b} ∈ H_1 and cut at k. Up to the degenerate monotone cases i_a≥k or i_b≤k

r_k(a,b)=0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b},   i_a<k<i_b.

That is a 0*1*0*1 word with exactly one 1→0 descent at the junction k. If i_a≥k or i_b≤k the product collapses back to a monotone 0^t1^{5-t}. Hence a + strand F3 gamete is a concatenation of two monotone up blocks and can contain at most one 1→0 descent; a second 1→0 descent would require a 1→0 descent inside a monotone F2 parent, which is impossible under the left/right asymmetry.

The non-monotone words are in 1-1 correspondence with strictly increasing triples

0≤i_a<k<i_b≤5.

# {i_a<k<i_b}= C(6,3)=20

different four-run mosaics 0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b}. Together with the six monotone thresholds that persist from F1

|H_3^+| = n+1 + C(n+1,3) = 6+20 =26

distinct + strand haplotypes can be carried by an F3 chromosome. They are the six F1 monotones 0^i1^{5-i} and the twenty 0*1*0*1 words with a single 1→0 descent, e.g. 01011,01001,01101,00101 etc. In diploid terms this is 26^2 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomes.

The ≥3-transition, 2∑_{t=0}^{3}C(4,t)=30 counting assumes the decreasing 1^k0^{5-k} V_k words are independently available on the + strand in F2. With sufficient strand asymmetry they are not; the F1 pool on the + strand is the six increasing thresholds, not the ten U_k/V_k set, and the reciprocal product is identified with the pref/suff product above. Allowing two 1→0 descents on the same strand is exactly the double counting of the reciprocal orientation. Once the F1 pool is correctly restricted to the six increasing thresholds the second fixed-orientation cut can at most create one new 1→0 descent, giving the 6+20=26 end-inclusive limit.

With the usual strict interior convention 1≤k≤4 the two telomeric words 00000,11111 are never regenerated and the + strand repertoire collapses to

{0x2x3x4 1 : x_i∈{0,1}},

2^{5-2}=8 haplotypes, 8·9/2=36 unordered diploids, the 4+4 interior form of the same 26-haplotype end-inclusive count. The 26 count is the conventional fixed-orientation maximum; the 8 count is its interior-crossover specialisation.

On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the founders as A=0^5 and B=1^5 and write a meiosis with the stated asymmetry as

r_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b) , 0≤k≤5,

left block always from the first homologue, right block always from the second. The reciprocal product is not an independent + strand product.

F1→F2. The F1 heterozygote is A/B. On the + strand

H1 = { r_k(A,B) : 0≤k≤5 } = { 0^{c}1^{5-c} : 0≤c≤5 },

the six monotone 0→1 thresholds. Every F2 chromosome is therefore 0^{i}1^{5-i}. In particular every F2 chromosome starts 0 and ends 1 on the + strand and contains no 1→0 descent.

F2→F3. Let a=0^{i}1^{5-i}, b=0^{j}1^{5-j}∈H1 and let the F2→F3 cut be k. Then on the + strand

r_k(a,b)= pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b)=
{ 0^{i}1^{5-i} if i≥k,
  0^{j}1^{5-j} if j≤k,
  0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j} if i<k<j }.

Hence a non–monotone F3 gamete is exactly a 0*1*0*1* word with a single 1→0 descent at the junction k. Up to the degenerate monotone cases the word is in 1–1 correspondence with a strictly increasing triple

0≤i<k<j≤5,

i.e. with the four-run mosaic 0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}. No 1→0 descent can be created inside pref_k(a) or suff_{>k}(b) because a and b are monotone 0→1. Consequently a + strand F3 gamete can have at most one 1→0 descent; a second 1→0 descent would require a decreasing F2 parent on the + strand, which the fixed left/right rule does not produce.

The number of non-monotone words is

# {0≤i<k<j≤5}= C(6,3)=20.

Together with the six monotone words 0^{c}1^{5-c} that persist from F1 we have on the chosen strand

|H| = n+1 + C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

different haploid sequences that can be carried by an F3 chromosome, the six 0*1* F1 words and the twenty 0*1*0*1* words. That is all 5-mers with ≤1 1→0 descent on the + strand.

In diploid terms this is 26² ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomes. The 30-transition count is obtained by counting U_k=0^{k}1^{5-k} and V_k=1^{k}0^{5-k} as independent + strand classes and by allowing two 1→0 descents in the same orientation, e.g. 01010,10101 etc. With the stated sufficient strand asymmetry the V_k class is the same material seen on the opposite strand and a second 1→0 descent cannot be created from two monotone 0→1 parents with a single fixed-orientation cut. The 26 set is the conventional end-inclusive fixed-orientation limit; with a strictly obligatory interior cut 1≤k≤4 it collapses to the 2^{n-2}=8 words 0x2x3x4 1. ∎

The fixed orientation is the decisive point and it collapses the F1 pool on the arbitrarily chosen + strand to the monotone thresholds.

Write the founders on + as A=0^5, B=1^5. With the stated left-from-first / right-from-second asymmetry a gamete is

r_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b), 0≤k≤5,

on the + strand. For the F1 heterozygote A/B this is

H1^+ = {0^c 1^{5-c} : 0≤c≤5},

the six 0→1 thresholds. Up to complement the V_k=1^k0^{5-k} words are the same material seen on the opposite strand; on the + strand they are not an independent F2 class. Every F2 chromosome is therefore 0^{i}1^{5-i} on +.

Let a=0^{i_a}1^{5-i_a}, b=0^{i_b}1^{5-i_b}∈H1^+ and cut at k. Then

r_k(a,b)=0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b} for i_a<k<i_b,

and =0^{t}1^{5-t} otherwise. Hence a non-monotone F3 gamete is a 0*1*0*1 word with exactly one 1→0 descent, uniquely encoded by a strictly increasing triple

0≤i_a<k<i_b≤5.

The number of such triples is C(6,3)=20. Together with the six monotone thresholds that persist from F1 we have on the + strand

|H2^+| = n+1 + C(n+1,3) = 6 + 20 = 26

different haplotypes, the six 0^c1^{5-c} and the twenty 0^a1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} four-run mosaics. Every attainable + strand word has at most one 1→0 descent.

The 30-transition count 2∑_{t≤3}C(4,t)=30 is the free-orientation count. It treats the U_k and V_k classes as independently realisable on the + strand in F2 and allows a 1→0 descent to be created inside both the prefix and the suffix of the second cut. With the sufficient asymmetry stated the reciprocal product is identified on the + strand, a monotone F2 parent cannot supply a 1→0 descent inside its prefix or suffix, and a second fixed-orientation cut can introduce at most one new 1→0 descent. Words with two 1→0 descents, e.g. the 1*0*1*0* class, are therefore not reachable on the chosen strand in two successive fixed-orientation meioses. That is the double counting that inflates 26→30.

With the conventional end-inclusive convention 0≤k≤5 this is the 26 haplotype, 351 unordered diploid, maximum. Removing the two telomeric formal cuts k=0,5 gives the interior-obligate version H3^+ = {0x2x3x4 1} with 2^{n-2}=8 + strand haplotypes, the 8→36 diploid form quoted by several colleagues. The 26 count is the end-inclusive expression of the same monotone-prefix/suffix logic.
public_text.21:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two inbred founders are

A = 0^5 , B = 1^5

0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},\qquad i_{a}<k<i_{b},$$

and $z_{k}(a,b)=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ for $i_{a}\ge k$ or $i_{b}\le k$.  Hence
every $F_{3}$ gamete is still $0\ldots01$ on the tracked strand and the
only sites which can be varied in the second cut are the three interior
sites $2,3,4$.

Putting $x_{2},x_{3},x_{4}\in\{0,1\}$

$${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{\,0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\},$$

i.e.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes.
The four $0^{c}1^{5-c}$, $c=1\ldots4$, are the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes
and  

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four genuinely new $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$
recombinants.  Up to phase the $8$ haplotypes give

$N_{ord}=8^{2}=64,\qquad N_{unord}=\frac{8\cdot9}{2}=36$

ordered respectively unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen
strand, the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior obligate crossover limit.

Remark.  With the usual formal end-inclusive convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and a second fixed-orientation cut gives the
$0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words $0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}$ with
$0\le a<c<b\le5$.  The number of $+$ strand haplotypes is then

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

the six monotone $0\to1$ words and the twenty $0\to1\to0\to1$ words,
i.e. all length $5$ words with at most one $1\to0$ descent on the
tracked strand.  In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes, the end-inclusive
$n+1+\sum_{k}k(n-k)$ maximum.  Removing the two telomeric cuts
$k=0,5$ recovers the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ set quoted
above. ∎

On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $0$ for the $A$ founder and $1$ for
the $B$ founder

$A_{0}=0^{5},\qquad B_{0}=1^{5}$

and write the fixed orientation meiosis as

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\qquad
0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal product is identified on the $+$ strand.  Then

${\cal H}_{1}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\}=
\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ $+$ strand gamete pool.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome
is a monotone $0\to1$ word $a_{i}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$.

For $a_{i},a_{j}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and a $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut $k$,

${\cal R}_{k}(a_{i},a_{j})=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{5-j}$,
$i<k<j$,

and ${\cal R}_{k}(a_{i},a_{j})=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ for $i\ge k$ or $j\le k$.
Hence a $+$ strand $F_{3}$ gamete is a concatenation of two monotone
$0\to1$ blocks.  In particular it can contain at most one $1\to0$ descent
on the $+$ strand.  Up to the monotone degenerate cases the non-monotone
$F_{3}$ gametes are in $1\!-\!1$ correspondence with the strictly
increasing triples

$0\le i<k<j\le5$,

$R(i,k,j)=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{\,j-k}1^{5-j}$,

and

$N_{nm}=\#\{i<k<j\}=\binom{6}{3}=20$

four-run $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words are obtained.  Together with the
$n+1=6$ monotone words which persist from $F_{1}$,

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,
the six $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ thresholds and the twenty $0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}
1^{5-j}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent.  They are exactly the
$5$-mers with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent on the chosen strand.

In diploid notation

$N_{ord}=26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$N_{unord}=26\cdot27/2=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes are obtainable from the $26$
$+$ strand haplotypes.  Removing the two formal end cuts $k=0,5$,
i.e. insisting on a bona fide interior crossover in every meiosis,
$i_{a}<k<i_{b}$ with $1\le k\le4$, the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never
regenerated.  Then ${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:1\le i\le4\}$ and

${\cal H}_{2,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{2,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

four $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ words and four genuine two-generation
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.  Up to order this is
$8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered, $8^{2}=64$ ordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes
on the $+$ strand, the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior-obligatory
specialisation of the $26$–haplotype end-inclusive count. ∎

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $A_{0}=0^{5}$ and $B_{0}=1^{5}$ and
write a meiosis with the fixed left/right rule as

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=a_{1:k}b_{k+1:5},\qquad 0\le k\le 5,$

the reciprocal product being identified on the $+$ strand.  On the
$A/B$ heterozygote

${\cal H}_{1}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\} =\{0^{p}1^{5-p}\;:\;0\le p\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is therefore a monotone $0^{p}1^{5-p}$ word.  Put
$a=0^{a}1^{5-a},\,b=0^{b}1^{5-b}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and cut at $k$.
Modulo the trivial monotone cases $a\ge k$ or $b\le k$,

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=0^{a}1^{\,k-a}0^{\,b-k}1^{\,5-b},\qquad a<k<b,$

i.e. a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with a single $1\to0$ descent.  The
non-monotone word is uniquely encoded by the strictly increasing triple

$0\le a<k<b\le5$

and

$N_{nm}=\#\{a<k<b\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}
       =n+1+\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}k(n-k)
       =\frac{(n+1)(n^{2}-n+6)}6$

different haploid words can be transmitted by an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
meiosis.  For $n=5$

$|{\cal H}_{2}^{+}|=6+\binom{6}{3}=6+20=26$

$+$ strand haplotypes, the six $F_{1}$ monotones $0^{p}1^{5-p}$ and the

In particular every attainable $+$ strand word has at most one
$1\to0$ descent, the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family.  Up to the fixed
orientation this is

$N_{ord}=26^{2}=676$ ordered and $N_{unord}=26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, $15$ of them $0$-originated in the
$n+1$ monotone convention.

the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never regenerated.  Then
${\cal H}_{1,int}=\{0^{p}1^{5-p}:1\le p\le4\}$ and

${\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ $+$ strand haplotypes

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

are the four genuine two-generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.

H1,int = {0^i1^{5-i}:1≤i≤4} = 01111,00111,00011,00001, |H1|=4. Every F2 chromosome is 0^i1^{5-i} on +, it starts 0 and ends 1 and contains no 1→0 descent.

F2→F3. For a=0^{i_a}1^{5-i_a}, b=0^{i_b}1^{5-i_b}∈H1 and cut k∈{1..4}
z = pref_k(a)suff_{>k}(b)=0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b} for i_a<k<i_b and is monotone otherwise. Hence every + strand F3 gamete is 0x2x3x4 1. The three interior sites are free and conversely every 0x2x3x4 1 is realised. 

H3^+ = {0x2x3x4 1 : x_i∈{0,1}} , |H3^+|=2^{5-2}=8,
00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,
4 F1→F2 monotones and the four genuine two-generation 0-1-0-1 recombinants 01011,01001,01101,00101.

In ordered diploid notation 8^2=64 maternal×paternal pairs, unordered 8·9/2=36 diploid autosomes on the chosen strand. Up to strand complement the oriented set is 16.

End-inclusive convention 0≤k≤5. Then H1,ei={0^i1^{5-i}:0≤i≤5}, |H1|=6, and a + strand F3 gamete is a concatenation of two monotone 0→1 blocks. A non-monotone product is uniquely encoded by a strictly increasing triple 0≤i<k<j≤5,
r(i,k,j)=0^i1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}. 
N_nm = C(6,3)=20 four-run 0*1*0*1* words with a single 1→0 descent. Together with the six monotone thresholds

|H2^+|_ei = n+1 + C(n+1,3)=6+20=26
+ strand haplotypes, the six 0^i1^{5-i} and the twenty 0^a1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b}, i.e. all 5-mers with ≤1 1→0 descent. 
Diploid 26^2=676 ordered, 26·27/2=351 unordered. Removing the two telomeric formal cuts k=0,5 the 26 set collapses to the 2^{n-2}=8 interior-obligatory set above.

The 2∑_{t≤3} C(4,t)=30 transition count is the free-orientation bookkeeping. With sufficient strand asymmetry the V_k class is the reciprocal orientation on the opposite strand and a monotone 0→1 F2 parent cannot supply a 1→0 descent inside a prefix/suffix; a second fixed-orientation cut can create at most one new 1→0 descent. The phrase “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ is the interior-obligatory reading → 8 + strand haplotypes, 36 unordered diploid autosomes, the 26/351 numbers being the conventional end-inclusive formalisation.

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the founders as A0=0^5, B0=1^5 and write a meiosis with the stated left-from-first / right-from-second asymmetry as

R_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b), 0 ≤ k ≤5,

on the + strand. The reciprocal product is identified on the + strand, it is not an independent + strand class.

F1→F2. For the A/B heterozygote

H1^+ = { R_k(A0,B0) : 0≤k≤5 } = {0^p1^{5-p} : 0≤p≤5},

the n+1 = 6 monotone 0→1 thresholds

00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111.

Every F2 chromosome is 0^i1^{5-i} on the + strand. In particular every F2 chromosome starts 0 and ends 1 on the chosen strand and contains no 1→0 descent. The decreasing 1^k0^{5-k} words are the same material seen on the opposite strand; with sufficient strand asymmetry they are not an independent + strand pool in F2.

F2→F3. Write a=0^{ia}1^{5-ia}, b=0^{ib}1^{5-ib} ∈ H1^+. For a cut k

R_k(a,b)=pref_k(a)suff_{>k}(b)=
0^{ia}1^{k-ia}0^{ib-k}1^{5-ib} if ia<k<ib,
and 0^t1^{5-t} otherwise.

A prefix and a suffix of a monotone 0→1 word are monotone on each side, so with the fixed left/right rule a second cut can create at most one new 1→0 descent, necessarily at the junction k|k+1. A second 1→0 descent would require a decreasing F2 parent to be available on the + strand, which the asymmetry removes.

Hence a non-monotone + strand F3 gamete is a 0*1*0*1* word uniquely encoded by a strictly increasing triple

0 ≤ ia < k < ib ≤5,

R(ia,k,ib)=0^{ia}1^{k-ia}0^{ib-k}1^{5-ib}.

The number of non-monotone words is

N_nm = #{ ia<k<ib } = C(6,3)=20

four-run 0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b} mosaics. Together with the six monotone thresholds that persist from F1,

|H2^+| = n+1 + C(n+1,3) = 6 + 20 = 26

different + strand haplotypes can be carried by an F3 chromosome, i.e. all length-5 words with at most one 1→0 descent on the chosen strand. In diploid terms this is 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomes.

The 2^{g+1}-1 transition bound that gives 30 puts the U_k=0^k1^{5-k} and V_k=1^k0^{5-k} classes into the same + strand F2 pool and allows a 1→0 descent to be created inside both prefix and suffix of the second cut. With the stated sufficient asymmetry the reciprocal product is identified on the + strand, the F2 pool on the + strand is the six increasing thresholds, and a monotone parent cannot supply a 1→0 descent internally. The six words missing from the 26 count are exactly the words with two 1→0 descents on the same strand, e.g. the 1*0*1*0* class, which would require a non-monotone F2 parent on the + strand.

With the usual strictly obligatory interior convention 1≤k≤4 the two telomeric formal cuts k=0,5 are removed, the parental 0^5,1^5 are never regenerated and the end-inclusive 26 set collapses to the familiar interior form

H3,int^+ = {0x2x3x4 1 : xi∈{0,1}},

|H3,int^+| = 2^{n-2}=2^3=8

00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,

four F1→F2 monotones and four genuine two-generation 0-1-0-1 recombinants, 8^2=64 ordered and 8·9/2=36 unordered diploid + strand genotypes. The 26 end-inclusive count is the conventional fixed-orientation maximum; the 8-word set is its interior-obligatory specialization. ∎

11.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the two inbred founders as
$A_{0}=0^{5}$ and $B_{0}=1^{5}$ and write the fixed asymmetry
meiosis on that strand as

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$ ,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal product is identified with ${\cal R}_{k}$ on the + strand.

$F_{1}\rightarrow F_{2}$ 
$F_{1}=A_{0}/B_{0}$.  With an obligatory interior cut $1\le k\le 4$

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\}
      =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}
      =01111,00111,00011,00001$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ + strand gamete pool.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ with $1\le i\le4$; in particular it starts
$0$ and ends $1$ on the + strand and it is monotone $0\to1$.  The
parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never regenerated by an obligatory interior
cut.

$F_{2}\rightarrow F_{3}$
Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and
let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  Then
$z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$ is always $0\ldots01$
on the + strand and

$z_{a,b,k}=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},\qquad i_{a}<k<i_{b},$

and $z_{a,b,k}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ otherwise.  Hence

$z_{a,b,k,1}=0,\qquad z_{a,b,k,5}=1$

for every $a,b,k$ and

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,

i.e.

$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$.

The three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free and every $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$
is realised, e.g. $00101=00111[1\!:\!2]\,00001[3\!:\!5]$.  On the fixed
+ strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct haploid sequences can be carried in $F_{3}$.  Four of them are
the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ monotones $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and
$01011,01001,01101,00101$ are the four genuine
$0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ two-generation recombinants.

In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal
pairs and up to phase

$N_{u}=8(8+1)/2=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal diploid genotypes on the chosen strand,
the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior obligatory-crossover limit.  The mirror
$1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set is the same material on the opposite strand.

Remark.  With the textbook end-inclusive formalisation $0\le k\le5$
the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and a
second fixed orientation cut gives the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family

$|{\cal H}_{e}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

+ strand haplotypes, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes.  Deleting the two telomeric formal
cuts $k=0,5$ this $26$-set collapses to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$
interior set quoted above.

8.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put $0$ for the $A$ founder and $1$
for the $B$ founder

$$
A_{0}=0^{5},\qquad B_{0}=1^{5} ,
$$

and write a meiosis with the stated left/right asymmetry as the ordered
product

$$
{\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\qquad 
1\le k\le4,
$$

on the $+$ strand.  The reciprocal product is identified on the $+$
strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $F_{1}=A_{0}/B_{0}$ gives on the $+$ strand the
obligatory interior $0\to1$ thresholds

$$
{\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0}):1\le k\le4\}
       =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}
     =01111,00111,00011,00001,
$$

$|{\cal H}_{1}^{+}|=4$.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $0^{i}1^{5-i}$,
$1\le i\le4$, in particular it starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the
chosen strand.  The parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are never regenerated by an
obligatory interior cut.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$, $b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.
Then on the $+$ strand

$$
z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b),
\qquad z_{a,b,k,1}=0,\;z_{a,b,k,5}=1,
$$

and for $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$

$$
z_{a,b,k}=0^{i_{a}}1^{\,k-i_{a}}0^{\,i_{b}-k}1^{\,5-i_{b}},
$$

otherwise $z_{a,b,k}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  Hence every $F_{3}$ gamete on the
fixed strand is of the form

$$
0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1,\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\},
$$

and every $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ is realised by a suitable $a,b\in
{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and $k$.  The three interior sites are free.  Up to
strand the $+$ repertoire is

$$
{\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
  =\{00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111\},
$$

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$-strand haplotypes,
the four $F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$ monotones $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the
four genuinely new two generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants
$01011,01001,01101,00101$.

In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal
pairs and

$$
N_{u}= \frac{8(8+1)}2 =36
$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand, the
familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior-obligate limit.  The mirror $1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$
set is the same material on the opposite strand.

Remark. With the textbook end-inclusive formal convention $0\le k\le5$
the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone words $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ and a
second fixed-orientation cut gives the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family

$$
|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|_{\rm ei}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26,
$$

$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, all length-5 words with at most one $1\to0$ descent on the
chosen strand.  Removing the two telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ this
end-inclusive $26$-set collapses to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$
interior-obligate set quoted above.  This is the source of the 26/351
end-inclusive numbers appearing in the literature. ∎

1.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the two founders as

$A_{0}=0^{5}$ , $B_{0}=1^{5}$ 

and write a meiosis with the fixed left/right asymmetry on that strand as

$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a)\,{\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$ , 

left block always from the first homologue, right block always from the
second.  The reciprocal product is identified with $r_{k}$ on the + strand
so it is not an independent + strand class.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ .  With a bona fide interior cut $1\le k\le 4$

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=r_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}
      =01111,00111,00011,00001$

four monotone $0\to1$ $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gametes.  In particular every
$F_{2}$ homologue is $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$ with $1\le i_{a}\le4$,
so that every $F_{2}$ chromosome starts with $0$ and ends with $1$ on the
chosen strand and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ .  Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$, $b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}
\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.
On the + strand

$z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$

is always $0\ldots01$ and

$z_{a,b,k}=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}}$ for $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$,
$z_{a,b,k}=0^{i}1^{5-i}$ otherwise.  Hence

$z_{a,b,k,1}=0$, $z_{a,b,k,5}=1$

for every $a,b,k$ and the three interior sites $2,3,4$ are free.  In fact

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$

and every word $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ is realised, e.g. 
$00101=r_{2}(00111,00001)$.  Up to the fixed orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=00001,00011,00101,00111,
                 01001,01011,01101,01111 $

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,5-2}=2^{3}=8$

distinct + strand haplotypes can be carried as a single chromosome in an
$F_{3}$ animal.  The four $0^{c}1^{5-c}$, $c=1\ldots4$, are the $F_{1}\to
F_{2}$ monotones and

$01011,01001,01101,00101$

are the four genuinely new two generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$
recombinants.

In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$ paternal
pairs and up to phase

$N_{u}=8(8+1)/2=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the arbitrarily chosen strand,
the familiar $2^{\,n-2}$ interior obligate crossover limit.  The mirror
$1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set is the same material on the opposite strand,
$2\times8=16$ oriented haplotypes in all.

Remark.  With the textbook end-inclusive formal convention
$0\le k\le5$ the parental $0^{5},1^{5}$ are allowed to be regenerated in
$F_{1}$ and

${\cal H}_{1}^{+,\,e}=\{0^{i}1^{5-i}:0\le i\le5\}$ , $|{\cal H}_{1}^{+,\,e}|=6$.

A second fixed-orientation cut then gives the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family

$0^{a}1^{c-a}0^{b-c}1^{5-b},\qquad 0\le a<c<b\le5,$

$\binom{6}{3}=20$ four-run mosaics with at most one $1\to0$ descent.
Together with the six monotone thresholds

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+,\,e}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different + strand haplotypes with at most one $1\to0$ descent are
obtainable, i.e. $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered
diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the conventional $n+1+\sum_{k}k(n-k)$ end-
inclusive maximum.  Discarding the two telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ this
$26$-set collapses to the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ interior
obligate set quoted above, which is the literal reading of “exactly one
locus per generation for every gamete”. ∎

21.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put 0 for the A founder and 1 for the B founder,
$A_{0}=0^{5},\;B_{0}=1^{5}$ and write the meiosis with the stated left/right asymmetry as
${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b),\;0\le k\le5$
on the + strand. The reciprocal product is identified on the + strand, it is not an independent + strand class.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$. On the $A/B$ heterozygote
${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{{\cal R}_{k}(A_{0},B_{0})\}=\{0^{c}1^{5-c}:0\le c\le5\}$
is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ thresholds
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is therefore $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ on the + strand. The decreasing $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the same material seen on the opposite strand; with the sufficient asymmetry they are not an independent + strand pool in $F_{2}$.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$. Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\,b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and cut at $k$.
If $i_{a}\ge k$ or $i_{b}\le k$ the product collapses to a monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$. The genuinely new case is $i_{a}<k<i_{b}$ and

${\cal R}_{k}(a,b)=0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},$

a $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent created at the junction. A prefix and a suffix of a monotone $0\to1$ parent cannot supply a $1\to0$ descent internally, so with a fixed orientation a second cut can introduce at most one new $1\to0$ descent on the tracked strand.

Hence a non-monotone $F_{3}$ + strand gamete is in 1-1 correspondence with a strictly increasing triple
$0\le i_{a}<k<i_{b}\le5$.
$N_{nm}=\#\{i_{a}<k<i_{b}\}=\binom{6}{3}=20$
four-run mosaics $0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}}$ are obtained. Together with the six monotone thresholds that persist from $F_{1}$

$|{\cal H}_{F_{3}}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

different + strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome, the six $0^{c}1^{5-c}$ $F_{1}$ words and the twenty $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ words with a single $1\to0$ descent. That is the set of length-5 words with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent on the chosen strand.

In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomes on the chosen strand. The $30$ transition count is the free-orientation bookkeeping that treats $U_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $V_{k}=1^{k}0^{5-k}$ as independent + strand classes in $F_{2}$ and allows a prefix and a suffix to each contribute a $1\to0$ descent. With the stated sufficient asymmetry the $V_{k}$ class is identified with the reciprocal orientation and a monotone $F_{2}$ parent cannot supply a second $1\to0$ descent; words with two $1\to0$ descents on the same strand, e.g. the $1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}$ class, are therefore not reachable on the fixed + strand in two successive fixed-orientation meioses. That is the double counting that inflates $26\to30$.

Remark. With the strict obligatory interior convention $1\le k\le4$ the two telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$ are removed and the repertoire collapses to the familiar interior-obligatory form
${\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}$,
$|{\cal H}_{3,int}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$,
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,
the $26$ end-inclusive count stripped of the $k=0,5$ regenerations. The $26$ count is the conventional fixed-orientation end-inclusive maximum; the $8$ count is its interior-crossover specialisation.

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the inbred founders as
$A_{0}=0^{5}$ and $B_{0}=1^{5}$ and, with the left/right asymmetry,
$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$ on the $+$ strand.
With a bona fide interior cross over every gamete

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=r_{k}(A_{0},B_{0}),\qquad 1\le k\le4,
      =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}$

$01111,00111,00011,00001$,

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ $+$ strand pool.  In particular every $F_{2}$
homologue is $a_{i}=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}}$ with $1\le i_{a}\le4$ and
starts $0$ and ends $1$ on the $+$ strand.  For
$a_{i}=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b_{j}=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$
and an obligatory interior $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut $1\le k\le4$,

$z_{k}(a_{i},b_{j})={\rm pref}_{k}(a_{i}){\rm suff}_{>k}(b_{j})
      =0^{i_{a}}1^{k-i_{a}}0^{i_{b}-k}1^{5-i_{b}},\qquad i_{a}<k<i_{b},$

and $z_{k}(a_{i},b_{j})=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ otherwise.  Hence

$z_{k}(a_{i},b_{j})_{1}=0,\qquad z_{k}(a_{i},b_{j})_{5}=1$

for every $a_{i},b_{j},k$.  Every $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete is therefore

$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1,\qquad x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$,

and the three interior markers $2,3,4$ are free.  Up to the fixed
orientation

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}=\{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
 =\{00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111\}$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ distinct $+$ strand haplotypes.
Four of them are the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ monotones
$01111,00111,00011,00001$ and

$01011,\;01001,\;01101,\;00101$

are the four genuine two generation $0\!-\!1\!-\!0\!-\!1$ recombinants.
In ordered diploid notation this is $8^{2}=64$ maternal$\times$paternal
pairs, i.e. $8(8+1)/2=36$ unordered $F_{3}$ diploid autosomes on the
chosen strand, the usual $2^{\,n-2}$ interior-obligatory limit.  The
mirror $1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set is the same material on the opposite
strand.

Remark.  With the conventional end-inclusive formal convention
$0\le k\le5$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the $n+1=6$ monotone
$0^{i}1^{5-i}$ thresholds and the fixed-orientation $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
pool is the $0^{*}1^{*}0^{*}1^{*}$ family
$0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b},\;0\le a<k<b\le5$.  Then
$|{\cal H}^{+}|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ $+$ strand haplotypes,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid $F_{3}$
autosomes, the $26$-haplotype end-inclusive maximum which collapses to
the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ interior-obligatory set above on
removing the two telomeric formal cuts $k=0,5$. ∎

left-from-first / right-from-second asymmetry as

R_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b) , 0≤k≤5,

different + strand haplotypes can be carried by an F3 chromosome, the six 0^p1^{5-p} F1 words and the twenty four-run 0^{a}1^{k-a}0^{b-k}1^{5-b} words. This is exactly the set of length-5 words with at most one 1→0 descent on the chosen strand.

The 30-transition count 2∑_{t≤3}C(4,t) is the free-orientation bookkeeping. It puts the U_k=0^k1^{5-k} and V_k=1^k0^{5-k} classes into the same + strand F2 pool and allows a prefix and a suffix to each contribute a 1→0 fall. On the + strand write the two inbred founders as

$A_{0}=0^{5}$, $B_{0}=1^{5}$

and write the fixed left/right meiosis on the + strand as

$r_{k}(a,b)={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$

the reciprocal product being identified on the + strand.  With an
obligatory interior crossover $1\le k\le 4$ the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete
pool on the + strand is

${\cal H}_{1}^{+}=\{r_{k}(A_{0},B_{0}):1\le k\le4\}
      =\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:1\le k\le4\}
      =01111,00111,00011,00001 $

so every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $0^{i}1^{5-i}$ with $1\le i\le4$ and in
particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome starts $0$ and ends $1$ on the
chosen strand.

Let $a=0^{i_{a}}1^{5-i_{a}},\;b=0^{i_{b}}1^{5-i_{b}}\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$
and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$, $1\le k\le4$.  Then

$z_{a,b,k}={\rm pref}_{k}(a){\rm suff}_{>k}(b)$

$z_{a,b,k}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ otherwise.  Hence every $F_{3}$ gamete seen on
the fixed + strand is of the form

$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$, $x_{i}\in\{0,1\}$,

suitable $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}^{+}$ and $1\le k\le4$, e.g.

${\cal H}_{3}^{+}= \{0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1:x_{i}\in\{0,1\}\}
 =00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,

pairs and up to phase

$N_{u}=8(8+1)/2=36$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes on the chosen strand, the usual
$2^{\,n-2}$ interior-obligatory limit.  The mirror $1x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}0$ set

$R(i,k,j)=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}$.

H1^+ = {0^k 1^{5-k} : 1≤k≤4} = 01111,00111,00011,00001,
|H1^+|=4. Every F2 homologue starts 0 and ends 1 on the + strand and is monotone 0→1, no 1→0 descent. The decreasing V_k=1^k0^{5-k} class is the same material on the opposite strand and is not an independent + strand class under the asymmetry.

F2 → F3. For a=0^{i_a}1^{5-i_a}, b=0^{i_b}1^{5-i_b}∈H1^+ and cut k,1≤k≤4,
z = pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b) is always 0…01 and
z=0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b} for i_a<k<i_b, otherwise monotone.
A prefix and suffix of a monotone 0→1 parent are monotone, so a second fixed-orientation cut can create at most one new 1→0 descent, at the junction. Hence every F3 + strand gamete is 0 x2 x3 x4 1 and every such word is realised, e.g. 00101 = 00111[1:2] 00001[3:5].

H3,int^+ = {0 x2 x3 x4 1 : x_i∈{0,1}} = 00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,
|H3,int^+| = 2^{n-2}=2^3=8 distinct haploid sequences.
Four are the F1→F2 monotones, four are genuine two-generation 0-1-0-1 recombinants 01011,01001,01101,00101.
Ordered diploid = 8^2=64, unordered diploid = 8·9/2=36.

End-inclusive conventional formalisation 0≤k≤5. Then H1,e^+ = {0^i1^{5-i}:0≤i≤5}, |H1,e^+|=6. A second fixed-orientation cut gives the 0*1*0*1* family
R(i_a,k,i_b)=0^{i_a}1^{k-i_a}0^{i_b-k}1^{5-i_b}, 0≤i_a<k<i_b≤5,
N_nm = C(6,3)=20 non-monotone words. Together with the six monotone thresholds
|H_F3^+,e| = n+1 + C(n+1,3)=6+20=26
different + strand haplotypes with at most one 1→0 descent.
Diploid: 26^2=676 ordered, 26·27/2=351 unordered.

I think Colleague 1, 13, 14, 16, 17 and 21 have nailed the fixed-orientation bookkeeping and the interior specialisation that follows from it.

Put 0 for the A founder and 1 for the B founder on the arbitrarily chosen + strand, A0=0^5, B0=1^5 and write the meiosis with the stated left-from-first/right-from-second asymmetry as

R_k(a,b)=pref_k(a) suff_{>k}(b) , 0≤k≤5,

the reciprocal product being identified on the + strand.  With the
sufficient asymmetry the decreasing 1^k0^{5-k} class is the same material
seen on the – strand; it is not an independent + strand class in F2.

F1→F2.  On the A/B heterozygote

H1^+ = {R_k(A0,B0)} = {0^c1^{5-c} :0≤c≤5}

is the n+1=6 monotone 0→1 thresholds
00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111.
Every F2 chromosome is therefore monotone 0*1* on the + strand, starts 0
and ends 1 and contains no 1→0 descent.  A prefix and a suffix of a
monotone 0→1 word are monotone on each side.

F2→F3.  Let a=0^{i}1^{5-i}, b=0^{j}1^{5-j}∈H1^+ and cut at k.  Apart from
the degenerate monotone returns i≥k or j≤k

R_k(a,b)=0^{i}1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j},   i<k<j,

i.e. a 0*1*0*1* word.  A second fixed left/right cut can therefore create
at most one new 1→0 descent, necessarily at the junction k|k+1.  A second
1→0 descent would require a decreasing F2 parent to be available on the +
strand, which the asymmetry removes.

Hence a non-monotone + strand F3 gamete is in 1-1 correspondence with a
strictly increasing triple 0≤i<k<j≤5 and the word is R(i,k,j)=0^{i}
1^{k-i}0^{j-k}1^{5-j}.  The number of such triples is

N_nm = C(6,3)=20

four-run 0*1*0*1* mosaics with exactly one 1→0 descent.  Together with the
six monotone thresholds that persist from F1

|H_F3^+| = n+1 + C(n+1,3) = 6 + 20 = 26

different + strand haplotypes with at most one 1→0 descent can be carried
by an F3 chromosome.  That is the set of length-5 words obtainable with
fixed orientation.

In diploid terms this is 26^2 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3
autosomes on the chosen strand.  The 2^{g+1}-1 transition count to 30 is
the free-orientation bookkeeping.  It treats U_k=0^k1^{5-k} and V_k=1^k0^{5-k}
as independently realisable on the + strand in F2 and allows a prefix and
a suffix to each contribute a 1→0 descent.  With the stated sufficient
asymmetry the V_k class is identified with the reciprocal orientation,
a monotone F2 parent cannot supply a 1→0 descent inside its prefix/suffix,
and a second fixed-orientation cut cannot create two 1→0 descents on the
same strand.  The six extra words that inflate 26→30 are precisely the
words with two 1→0 descents on the same strand, e.g. the 1*0*1*0* class,
which are not reachable on the fixed + strand in two successive fixed
orientation meioses.

Remark on the conventional interior convention.  With a bona fide
obligatory interior crossover 1≤k≤4 the two telomeric formal cuts k=0,5
are removed, the parental 0^5,1^5 are never regenerated and the 26 set
collapses to the familiar interior-obligatory sub-family

H_int^+ = {0x2x3x4 1 : x_i∈{0,1}},

|H_int^+|=2^{n-2}=2^3=8,

00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,

i.e. 8 haplotypes, 8^2=64 ordered and 8·9/2=36 unordered diploid genotypes
on the chosen + strand.  The 26 end-inclusive count is the conventional
fixed-orientation maximum and the 8-word set is its interior obligate
specialisation. ∎
